behavioral_effects: The joined graph (765 nodes, 1424 edges) materializes to a gitignored SQLite cache on scan, and two committed reports now stand: cycles.json finds two real Python cycles (rag connectors package cycle and the six-module services-worker cycle, both closed at module scope), orphans.json names 5 Python and 18 TypeScript modules with no importer and no explaining classification - including the unreachable resend and smtp email providers behind a match statement whose catch-all always selects the log provider.
The no-orphaned-surfaces rule left phase-3 deferral and now runs as an advisory check, alongside the new no-dependency-cycles rule; both fire on the current tree and both are advisory by design.
compatibility_impact: The dynamic-import detector now catches the bare import_module form, so app.services.rag is correctly a dynamic site; downstream this reclassifies its submodules as unknowable rather than orphaned, which is the accurate reading. No generated schema broke; two new internal schemas validate the reports.
follow_up: The 23 named orphans and 2 cycles are debt-sweep candidates, not this plan: notably the email provider selection bug where EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend silently gets the log provider.
Session 6.5 wires cross-language expansion into impact and measures the phase-6 exit criteria against the 6.0 baseline.
limitations: The orphan check covers the module slice of the rule statement; route and tool consumer analysis needs the phase-7 site join, and the reports read from extractors directly rather than the SQLite cache by design.
reason: The three extraction layers exist but nothing joins them: queries re-derive everything per process, the no-orphaned-surfaces rule has sat deferred since phase 3 for want of exactly this analysis, and cycles are invisible until someone introduces one; this materializes the joined graph as a cache and turns both analyses into committed reports with advisory checks
risks: Orphan exclusion classes were calibrated against the current tree; a new legitimate no-importer pattern (a plugin mechanism, a new framework convention) would surface as a false orphan until its class is added.
rollback: git revert of the single commit; also delete .cache/repo-governance/repository.sqlite if a stale cache should not linger, though nothing committed reads it.
security_impact: None. Analyses over already-extracted structure; the SQLite cache is gitignored and derived, and reports name modules only, never values.
summary: Store the graph in SQLite and report cycles and orphans
